F factor content of net imports

rationale: All five Table 10 output files were produced and their panel assignments confirmed from the do-file (do/czone_analysis_ipw_final.do, lines 284-290 d_tradex_usch_pw -> tab_expoff_iv = Panel B; 297+ d_tradeusch_netinput_pw -> tab_intermediates = Panel C; tab_nipw_iv = Panel D; tab_nipw_grav = Panel E gravity OLS; tab_ifactor_net_io = Panel F). Panel A (baseline) is the full-spec d_tradeusch_pw row assembled from tab_ipw_manuf_2.scsv/tab_ipw_empl.scsv (Mfg emp/pop -0.596, Nonmfg -0.178), tab_ipw_mfgnmfg.scsv (Mfg log wage 0.151, Nonmfg log wage -0.761), tab_ipw_trans.scsv (log transfers 1.013), tab_ipw_hhinc_pw.scsv (Avg log HH wage inc -2.142) -- every cell within <1% of the paper. Panels C (-0.491/-0.010/0.707/-0.414/0.842/-1.229), D (-0.453/-0.093/0.455/-0.473/0.729/-1.388), E (-0.289/-0.034/0.036/-0.261/0.526/-0.777) and F (-0.571/-0.119/0.592/-0.657/0.806/-1.698) each reproduce their paper rows within a few percent, and the sign/significance pattern (nonmfg wages negative, transfers positive, HH wage income negative) holds throughout. The lone exception is Panel B (tab_expoff_iv, domestic+intl exposure): its Mfg emp/pop coefficient is -0.415 vs the paper's -0.51 (18.6% relative error), and its entire row deviates by ~16-47% (Nonmfg emp/pop -0.063 vs -0.12; Mfg log wage 0.199 vs 0.16; Nonmfg log wage -0.429 vs -0.6; transfers 0.732 vs 0.87; HH wage inc -1.375 vs -1.77). Since only a trivial matplotlib install was applied (assess/fix_severity.json: no analysis-code changes), these are the authors' code as-shipped. With 30 of 36 cells matching within ~5% but all 6 Panel B cells landing in the 15-30%+ band, this is a partial match, not a full one.
